name: WCWF World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Already live when the [DEWF/WCWF] satire subset opens, held by "Hollywood" Hulk Hogan; changed hands twice across the run's nine chapters -- to Shane Douglas via a mid-match contract cash-in, and from Douglas to Nailz by no-show forfeit at the climactic Soul Doubt broadcast.

name: WCWF World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Created and awarded outright to Demolition by owner Ted DiBiase rather than won in a tournament final; the satire subset's own record shows one successful defense, retained by forfeit after an opponent injury.

name: DEWF World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The top prize of the Dream Extreme Wrestling Federation's 1997 comeback season, changing hands three times across nine weeks -- Kevin Nash's opening-night win over "The Franchise" Shane Douglas, a mystery-challenger swerve loss to Phil La Fon three weeks on, and Nash's own rematch win back three weeks after that -- before settling into a run of successful Nash defences that closes out this project's own read of the fed's 1997 corpus.

name: DEWF Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: "Outsider" Scott Hall's title through most of the fed's 1997 comeback season: won from The Giant on the season-opening show, retained through a stripping attempt by the fed's own (soon-departed) Commissioner, then declared vacant during a gap this project's own partition does not cover, and reclaimed by Hall in a three-way dance on the night a new Commissioner, "Nature Boy" Ric Flair, was installed.

name: DEWF World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Won on the fed's 1997 season-opening show by The Razor Boys (Al Perez & Paul Diamond) over Blondes 3:16, then lost two weeks later to The Road Warriors (Hawk & Animal) in a three-way dance also involving Blondes 3:16 -- a reign the Road Warriors were still defending, successfully, when this project's own read of the corpus closes out in October. A separate DEWF Trios Championship is name-checked as already standing (held jointly by The Razor Boys and Diamond Dallas Page) but no dated change for it survives in anything this project holds.

name: DEWF World Light Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: "The Shadow" Michael Monroe's title for the whole of this project's own read of the fed's 1997 season, successfully defended against a touring Michinoku Pro rookie in August; no loss is recorded in anything this project holds.
